accuracy.evidence: Every grapheme and example word was checked against English Appendix 1 of the National Curriculum in England: Year 1 lists ou (out, about, mouth, sound), ow for both sounds (now, how, brown, down, town; own, blow, snow, grow, show), ue and ew (blue, clue, glue, true; new, few, grew, flew, drew), ie as igh (lie, tie, pie, cried), aw and au (saw, draw, yawn, crawl; author, August, dinosaur) and -y as ee (very, happy, funny, party); Year 2 adds y as igh at the end (cry, fly, dry, try, reply, July). The adult text keeps the phonetic distinction honest: only ow in cow, ie, y in my and ow in snow glide, while ew, ue, aw and au are long vowels, and it flags the North American accent difference for aw and au and the July and reply exceptions to the beat rule.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips named in the adult text: reading every ow as in cow (step 1 prediction 'Yes, the same', challenge town for grow, practice p1), thinking different letters must make different sounds (step 2 prediction, mastery m2 cloud and cow), wrong spelling for a shared sound (clowd and clawd in m5, clows and clewz in the challenge, gap step with five teams), y at the start read as a vowel (challenge yes, m4) and the beat rule for y endings (step 4 prediction, funny vs sky), plus homophones blue/blew, flower/flour, tied/tide with the meaning given for each wrong pick.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagglide is built on this topic's own problem, that one spelling can say two sounds and one sound can have two spellings: ow words go to cow or snow houses with feedback that says the word both ways, nine words go to shared-sound houses that each hold two spellings, a vowel team tile is dropped into a word gap from a meaning clue (with real-word feedback for flow, flaw, paw, caw, pew), y words are sorted by clapped beats with beat dots shown, and sound-alike words are chosen by meaning. lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab, including flagvowel and flagrvowel.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child meets each rule by doing it before the summary: putting snow in the cow house returns 'Say snow with the cow sound: it is not a word. ow in snow says the sound in snow. ow has two sounds, so try both'; dropping ow into fl_ returns 'Water can flow, but a bird flew. flew needs ew'; the y houses list happy •• and fly • so the beat pattern is visible on the done screen. Done screens list every word with its team (cow: ow, flew: ew, claw: aw, cloud: ou, pie: ie).

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each hold the tempting wrong answer the step then disproves: that ow says one sound (step 1 sorts eight words into two houses), that cloud and cow cannot share a sound because the letters differ (step 2), that the y in my sounds like the y in happy (step 4 beat sort), and that blue and blew mean the same because they sound the same (step 5). The done line repeats the child's prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages, each naming the slip: cow sound vs snow sound (town, show), ew vs ow (grew), oo vs ow (shoot), aw vs ue (claw), two beats so y says ee (funny), y at the start is not a vowel (yes), ow and ew cannot spell claw (clows, clewz), blue is a colour not the past of blow, and blow vs blew for something that already happened.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short, concrete sentences (Say cow. Now say snow. Both have ow, but ow says a different sound in each.) and pass the family readability limit in validate_lessons. Canvas words are 26 to 30 px on white cards; one instruction line per round; the young class gives 56 px buttons. The adult text uses the precise terms grapheme-level vowel digraph, diphthong and long vowel, with curriculum year references.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including Vowel Digraphs, R-Controlled Vowel Sounds, Split Digraphs and Homophones. Every feedback line names the word and the letters; step texts are one rule and one example each.

mobile.evidence: Checked all six steps at 360 px (Android-size viewport, touch) in light and dark, before and after Show me: the word card, two or three houses with up to five words each, the five vowel team keys (ow ou ew aw ie) on one row, and the blew/blue keys all fit without clipping; house labels split onto two lines (ou ow / cow); the button row wraps cleanly under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed all five tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a labelled button ('cow: ow in snow', 'cloud: ou ow: cow', 'Put ew in the gap', 'happy: y says ee: happy', 'Fill the gap with blew'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line. Canvas text is dark ink on pale fills in both themes; the team tiles are #5b21b6 on #ede9fe.

Common Core State Standards ELA RF.1.3c and RF.2.3b (vowel teams)
